newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - UAL EPS estimates cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - UAL EPS estimates cut.

text.p: -- Gruntal & Co analyst Steve Lewins said Monday he cut his earnings estimates for UAL Corp, parent of United Airlines, to $3.25 a share from $3.50 for the third quarter and to $7.50 a share from $8.00 for full-year 1996.
-- He cited increased jet kerosene costs stemming from the recent U.S.-Iraqi confrontation and low oil inventories, as well as legal settlement costs with travel agents.

-- UAL and other major carriers recently raised fares, Lewins said. "The price hikes appear to be sticking without any impact on bookings, but it is too soon to be certain because UAL has a long booking curve. There probably will be little impact if any in September or the third quarter."

-- He added United's bookings suggest further volume improvement in September and, as a result, load factor should increase again. In August, UAL's load factor rose to 78.6 percent from 76.3 percent in August 1995.
-- "The breakeven load factor may increase more, though, due to fuel costs," Lewins said.
